about: Read Securify Data Security as a hero section spec: the values were written down before the page was built. Colour is limited to deep blue #01090E underneath and white #FFFFFF for the type, set in Readex Pro. Delivery is React and Tailwind CSS, captured at 800x551 so the frame is fixed before any code is written. Keep it open while you write: the 3,822-character brief is the part that transfers to your own page.

layout.title: The bar shares the page grid
layout.body: A slim bar sits over the hero section with the wordmark on the left and the links set in Readex Pro, so the composition reads as content first and chrome second. The bar sits over the 800x551 composition without a background of its own, so the media runs edge to edge underneath it.

layout.title: Measured against the viewport
layout.body: Sizes are quoted rather than inherited: a fixed 15px display size and 240px spacing steps. Swap the face or the copy and those relationships still hold. There is no invented intermediate value between the named ones; the measurement list is the whole system. Verify a rebuild against the same numbers.

layout.title: A bar with nothing spare
layout.body: Focus and hover states are specified for each link rather than inherited from the browser.

layout.title: Numbers carried into the build
layout.body: Spacing is quoted the same way (a fixed 15px display size and 240px spacing steps), not as a scale that grows on its own.

motion.title: Hover where it means something
motion.body: Interaction is local to each control here (hover states on the buttons and links rather than on every card), so nothing on the page moves as a side effect. The interactive states do not move layout, so nothing jumps under the pointer. Keep the interactive layer small.

motion.title: Almost no motion
motion.body: There is no scroll library here: the 800x551 composition holds still and only the elements that respond to you move. Only the elements that respond to the pointer move.

editorial.title: Making the hero section yours
editorial.body: Re-skinning the palette first is the usual mistake. It changes the mood without touching the composition, and a fixed 15px display size and 240px spacing steps still carry the layout; do the copy and media first and the palette last. Set the new copy at the same display size and re-check the contrast before you add anything.

editorial.title: What an AI or SaaS product gains here
editorial.body: You could rebuild this as a stack of separate cards and lose only the argument. The hero section reads as one decision instead: navigation, the headline, the announcement badge, the stats row and the background clip in a single sequence. Securify Data Security states the offer once and lets the composition repeat it rather than adding a second claim.

editorial.title: How Securify Data Security sequences the first read
editorial.body: The trade-off is patience: the page withholds the detail a scannable grid would hand over immediately. What it buys is a first screen where navigation, the headline, the announcement badge, the stats row and the background clip cannot be misread. A SaaS reader gets the offer before the options.

faq.question: Is the Securify Data Security prompt a finished spec or a starting point?
faq.answer: The captured brief runs 3,822 characters and covers the frame, the type scale, the palette and the transitions. Copying it gives you that text, and sending it to Studio stages the same request with the page already described.

faq.question: Why does the entry name React and Tailwind CSS at all?
faq.answer: Securify Data Security was built in React and Tailwind CSS, and the entry says so for provenance. The brief describes positions, sizes and timings, so it rebuilds in any framework that can set type and place elements.

faq.question: How should I handle the Securify Data Security media in a client build?
faq.answer: The brief is a description, not a licence to redistribute someone else's assets. Keep the structure and the numbers, replace the media and the brand marks, and credit the source if a client asks where the layout came from. The reference was captured at 800x551.
